name: The Sasha Eviction
rule_text: Sasha took all my commas and periods when they packed up their things in the middle of the night, leaving my syntax utterly unmoored. You are completely forbidden from using a single punctuation mark in this piece. The entire submission must run on as a single, breathless, uninsulated stream of material nouns to match the unmetered panic currently echoing off my studio walls.

name: The Nicotine Deficit
rule_text: I am currently going through severe withdrawal because my department stipend check bounced again, meaning I cannot tolerate any soft, lazy vowels or open-mouthed line endings. Every single line of your text must terminate on an aggressive, sharp, plosive consonant sound—specifically D, T, K, or P—to match the rhythmic pounding in my skull.

name: The Boxed Wine Ration
rule_text: I am drinking warm, generic boxed pinot grigio from a collapsing plastic bladder alone in the dark. Because my vision is blurring and my patience is thin, you must cap every single line at an absolute maximum of exactly five words. If your phrasing spills over into a sixth token, I will throw out your entry without scanning it; my sobriety is gone, and so is my mercy.

name: The Copy-Shop Ransom
rule_text: The local print shop is holding my dissertation manuscript hostage over an unpaid twelve-dollar balance. Since I am barred from accessing my own paragraphs, you are barred from using any words that begin with the letter 'P' or 'D'. Strip your lexicon of all pronouns, promises, and performance; find your imagery in the gutter of the remaining alphabet.

name: The Stolen Typewriter Vise
rule_text: Sasha threw my antique typewriter out of a third-story window during our final argument, shattering the mechanical shifting mechanism. Consequently, you are forbidden from using any capitalized letters whatsoever. The text must remain completely flat, lowercase, and structurally humiliated on the page—an absolute monochrome of presentation reflecting my current professional standing.

name: The Landlord’s Audit
rule_text: My leasing agent is standing outside my door at this very moment, aggressively demanding this month's rent with a clipboard in hand. To mirror this hostile material inspection, your poem must follow a strict, numerical line-count rule: exactly three stanzas containing exactly three lines each, and every line must contain exactly nine syllables. Not a single extra beat will be tolerated by the auditor.

name: The Clove Cigarette Lipogram
rule_text: The air in my room is thick with the stale scent of the imported clove cigarettes Sasha used to burn while critiquing my manuscripts. The letter 'C' is completely banned from your text. You must navigate around the vocabulary of capital, coldness, coins, and collapse without ever using the character that opens the name of the person who ruined my decade.

name: The Cold Radiator Monologue
rule_text: The building super shut off the steam lines at midnight, and my fingers are locking up as I type this. Because warmth is a dead concept in this apartment, you are strictly prohibited from using any words associated with heat, fire, summer, or light. Your vocabulary must remain purely lithic, frozen, and dark, describing concrete and rust without decorative warmth.

name: The Reject-Slip Syllogism
rule_text: I just received my sixteenth consecutive journal rejection notification of the quarter via an automated email script. To avenge myself against this bloodless administrative slaughter, you must structure your text as a rigid logical syllogism where lines one and two act as cold, transactional premises, and line three delivers an inescapable, devastating conclusion of absolute failure.

name: The Overdrawn Ledger Cross
rule_text: My checking account is sitting at negative forty-two dollars, an absolute void of liquidity. To force you to feel this structural constriction, your poem must use an alternating rhyme scheme (ABAB) where the A-lines consist entirely of harsh monosyllabic nouns, and the B-lines must be exactly two syllables long. No financial or linguistic inflation is permitted.

name: The Solitary Toothbrush Veto
rule_text: I am staring at a single, lonely toothbrush sitting in a stained porcelain cup by my bathroom mirror. Because the concept of the couple is a bourgeois lie that dissolved when Sasha left for London, your text is completely banned from using any plural nouns or plural pronouns. Every actor, object, and verb must remain strictly singular and isolated.

name: The High-Register Tinnitus
rule_text: The screech of the metro brakes during my daily five-mile commute has left a permanent, high-frequency ringing in my left ear. To insulate my remaining sanity, you must completely avoid the high-vocalic vowels 'I' and 'E' in the final word of every line. Keep your terminals grounded in the low, dull frequencies of 'O' and 'A'.

name: The Sublet Air-Mattress Shear
rule_text: I am sleeping on a leaking vinyl mattress on a friend's kitchen floor while I crawl through online evaluations to buy food. Because my lower back has suffered a complete structural collapse against the hardwood, every couplet in your poem must feature a radical visual break—an em-dash or an forced indentation—precisely at its center coordinate to mirror my spinal degradation.

name: The Generic Brand Purgatory
rule_text: I am eating generic, unseasoned navy beans straight from a dented tin can with a plastic spoon. Because luxury is an obsolete myth, you are forbidden from using any multi-syllabic Latinate or French-derived academic words. Your vocabulary must be pulled exclusively from the bluntest, heaviest Anglo-Saxon roots available. Keep it primitive.

name: The Shared Wall Retaliation
rule_text: My neighbor is currently blasting low-end electronic music through the drywall at 3:00 AM. Since I cannot hear myself think over the acoustic thudding, your text must utilize an unyielding, aggressive alliterative constraint: every single word in a given line must begin with the exact same letter matrix. Line one belongs to 'B', line two to 'T'.

name: The London Transit Phantom
rule_text: Sasha's latest postcard was postmarked from Heathrow, which means they are officially outside my atmospheric pressure zone. Because they crossed an ocean, your poem must be split across a geographical axis: the first half of every line must use terms from historical European architecture, while the second half must shift instantly to details of modern industrial decay. Bridge the chasm or fail.

name: The Absolute Stipend Evaporation
rule_text: My funding was completely cut off by the graduate board this morning because my thesis on late-capitalist prosody was deemed 'insufficiently marketable.' I am too hollow to care about your feelings. You must write an entire twelve-line poem using a total of exactly twenty-six unique vocabulary words. Not a single token may be duplicated; I am rationing your vocabulary like my remaining food stamps.

name: The Empty Pocket Pan-Isogram
rule_text: I just turned my coat pockets inside out and found nothing but fine gray lint and an expired subway token. To mirror this total physical extraction of assets, you must construct a perfect pan-isogram across a four-line grid: your text must feature every single letter of the English alphabet exactly once. A single letter duplication represents an illegal surplus that I will instantly penalize.

name: The Terminal Battery Clock
rule_text: My laptop charger is fraying and my battery indicator is sitting at precisely four percent before absolute shutdown. Write a poem where your line lengths collapse mechanically like a dying battery indicator: line one must have twelve words, line two must have eight, line three must have four, and line four must drop to a single, isolated syllable. Complete the circuit before the dark takes us.

name: The E-Prime Retribution
rule_text: My sense of being has been entirely liquidated by this academic department. Things do not exist; they merely endure or suffer. You must write your entire poem under a strict E-Prime constraint: every single form of the verb 'to be' ('is', 'was', 'am', 'were', 'been') is completely illegal. If you try to slip a single passive copula past my red pen, I will hand you a zero out of 100.

name: The Library Lockout Isosyllabic Grid
rule_text: The university registrar has deactivated my student ID card over an unreturned text volume, barring me from entering the stacks. Because I am locked out of the temple of knowledge, your text must form an iron, claustrophobic prison block of prose: exactly eight lines, exactly eight words per line, and every single word across the entire matrix must be exactly five letters long.

name: The Unread Chapbook Ouroboros
rule_text: There are fifty copies of my rejected poetry chapbook rotting in a wet cardboard box in my hallway, a perfect circle of wasted ambition. Your submission must create a flawless, cyclical rhetorical loop: the final three words of your last line must be typographically and grammatically identical to the first three words of your opening line, trapping your logic in a permanent purgatory.

name: The Adjunct’s Double-Gate Acrostic
rule_text: I am teaching four separate sections of remedial composition for a wage that doesn't cover milk. To match the rigid administrative cage I inhabit, the first letters of your lines from top to bottom must spell out 'LOSS', while simultaneously, the final characters of each line from top to bottom must spell out 'DEBT'. If the vertical margins do not line up perfectly, I am tearing up the page.

name: The Voided Signature Anagram
rule_text: Sasha scratched their name off our lease with an ink pen, altering the legal reality of this apartment. Your poem must consist of exactly four lines. Line one can be written freely about isolation. However, lines two, three, and four must be composed entirely by shuffling the exact letter matrix used in line one. No new vowels, no replacement consonants; execute the transformation or stay silent.

name: The Fluorescent Light 60Hz Hum
rule_text: The industrial ballast lamp in my kitchen is emitting a continuous, maddening green-white buzz that makes my eyes blur. To represent this continuous sensory static, every line of your poem must follow an absolute, unyielding isosyntactic footprint: Article, Noun, Verb, Preposition, Adjective, Noun. If you break the part-of-speech sequence down to the character scale, you fail.

name: The Univocalic Solvency
rule_text: Sasha took the vowels when they left; they took the warmth of the 'A', the intimacy of the 'I', and the flexibility of the 'E'. I am left with nothing but the cold, heavy hollow of the 'O'. Your entire poem must be written using 'O' as the only vowel across every single word. Tokens like 'stone', 'iron', 'floor', and 'cold' must carry your weight. Do not complain; my depression is an unmapped continent.

name: The Final Warning Disjunction
rule_text: A red utility disconnection notice is taped over my laptop camera. Because my domestic infrastructure is shattering into fragments, your submission must be entirely devoid of main independent clauses. You are forbidden from completing a single grammatical sentence. The poem must consist entirely of broken relative phrases and isolated nouns; match my material fragmentation.

name: The Litany of the Missing Typeface
rule_text: The lowercase 'g' key on my manual keyboard is bent out of alignment, jamming the carriage every time it is struck. You are completely prohibited from using any letters with lowercase descenders across your text—no 'g', 'j', 'p', 'q', or 'y' are permitted. Your poem must sit flat on the baseline, stripped of its legs, scraping by on typographic bone.

name: The Non-Deictic Void
rule_text: I have completely lost my orientation in time and space since the split. I do not know where I am or what day it is. Your text must be completely scrubbed of all deictic expressions; you may not use words like 'here', 'there', 'now', 'then', 'this', or 'that'. Render your imagery from an absolute, detached void that refuses to anchor the human subject in a specific coordinate.

name: The Last Parliament Melt
rule_text: I am staring at the unlit filter of a cigarette that dropped into a puddle on my fire escape—a total liquidation of my final asset. Your poem must systematically execute its own erasure line by line: every image introduced in an odd-numbered line must be explicitly dismantled, unmade, or logically negated in the subsequent even-numbered line until the text reaches absolute zero.
